title: Joining Wickliffe's band in 1920 and learning to arrange
summary: Levy plays violin in Wickliffe's jazz band at the Entertainers Cafe, teaches himself arranging from a library book, and recalls the trumpeters in the band.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Yeah, Jimmy Paloa. I know he lived down the street from me. When I was with Wickliffe's band here in 1920, Wickliffe's jazz band, I was playing violin, and Jimmy Paloa was playing plenty of sax. And he was playing off cello parts, and then they had living. See, that's where they did the orchestration. That was before they started arranging for the three saxophones, two altos and a tenor. And so I got to, I had finished the harmony course, you call it musicology, before my money stopped coming in and I had to stop studying. So I went down and got a book on arranging. I didn't have any money, so I went down to the public library and got a book on arranging, and studied it, and started making little arrangements for the band. And George Filae was playing trombone with him. He was one of the old bands, and he was one of the old New Orleans. You're talking about the 1920 band now?
1920, yes, 1920, Wickliffe's jazz. At Paradise. At the Paradise and also at the

N. Cheney's Cafe. And then later, I followed Carol Dickerson and Wyatt Houston, they were the violinists, and then Clarence Lee and I, we followed them in there. They went on and got in with another band.
Well, did you follow them with Wickliffe, or with? I was still with Wickliffe, yeah.
Wickliffe, they left Wickliffe to form a band of their own. Was that in the period that the
Schaffner was with Wickliffe? I was trying to remember.

Yeah, Schaffner, I remember, yeah, Schaffner played with us. And then we had Tommy Ladnere, and then another time. Schaffner played with us off and on many years. And one time his lip went bad, and I think we sent in your own, he didn't got Tommy Ladnere. And Red Allen. Oh, another time we had Red Allen playing with us. And little Ted McMurray. Remember him, little Ted McMurray? No. He was one of the nice little jazz trumpeters of that 1920s. And Did Sudler play with Wickliffe for a time? No, Sudler, Joe Sudler was with the band
